summary.headline: Deccan Gold Q1 FY27: Jonnagiri sold 59 kg gold for ~Rs87 Cr revenue, Rs6.35 Cr share of PAT; Rs137 Cr fundraise approved by Board.
summary.overview: Management said the June quarter established the company as a producer, led by Jonnagiri (Geomysore Services) gold production and first dore output from Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan). Jonnagiri sold about 59 kg of gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT, of which Deccan's share was Rs6.35 Cr; about 80 kg of gold equivalent sits in inventory. Management framed the company as having two verticals, gold and battery-metal critical minerals, and said Rs137 Cr of CCDs, equity and warrants is pending shareholder approval. Management said the next quarter should be much bigger, but margins were low in Q1 and the company asked for another quarter before giving clearer guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Gold inventory at quarter end (incl. dore)
financial_highlights.value: About 80 kg gold equivalent (40 kg gold + 60 kg dore)
Rs137 Cr via CCDs, equity shares and warrants

segments.name: Jonnagiri (Geomysore, gold, India)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales of 59 kg gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT; Deccan's share Rs6.35 Cr. Production about 1 kg/day, with 2,500 tpd expansion planned, targeting up to 2 tonnes/yr around FY29-30.

segments.name: Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan, gold)
segments.commentary: Dore production started via Merrill-Crowe; gravity circuit and leach circuit added. Full-scale commissioning expected soon; tailings of about 0.6 Mt at about 1.3 g/t for first 4-5 years of output.

segments.name: Kalevala (Finland, gold)
segments.commentary: Drilling to start around Sept 15; about 1,500 m planned. Kuikka mining lease pending; feasibility targeted in 2027; production seen 2028-29 or later with about 800 tpd plant.

segments.name: Critical minerals (Chhattisgarh nickel-copper-PGE, Bhalukona)
segments.commentary: 2,500 m drilled, 1.3 km mineralised zone identified; resource estimate and mining lease application targeted next year; 3,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Logrosan tungsten (Spain)
segments.commentary: About 3,000 m drilled; full Dehesa results expected mid-September, resource model by early October; 1,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Mozambique lithium-tantalum
segments.commentary: About 150 sq km, three licences; 200 tpd concentrator targeted by end-2027 or Q1 2028 for concentrate.

guidance_outlook: Jonnagiri FY27 production 500-600 kg (earlier guidance retained); FY28 750-800 kg. Management will confirm after next quarter.
Altyn Tor: about 150-160 kg in FY27 and 300-350 kg thereafter, per management comments.
Jonnagiri EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters; Q1 margins were significantly lower.
Altyn Tor revised mine design and life-of-mine plan by October 2026; underground resource above 5 Mt could extend mine life by 6-7 years.
Dividend from Geomysore unlikely in FY27 per management; may come next year, not guaranteed.
Capex: about Rs400-500 Cr per 1,000 tpd plant; Bhalukona 3,000 tpd about Rs650-700 Cr; Altyn Tor underground Rs150-200 Cr in 3-4 years; Jonnagiri shaft work possibly above Rs400 Cr in 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Jonnagiri processing approvals of 1,010 tpd, with expansion to 2,500 tpd being sought; Bhumi Puja done for expansion.
Altyn Tor leach circuit and new tailings dam (10-year life) under construction; commissioning date to be announced after Chairman-level visit next week.
Finland: about 1,500 m drilling from mid-September; Kuikka pit targets about 70 kg gold; underground mines planned.
Chhattisgarh: 15th drill hole under way; plan 3,000 tpd plant; process flow sheet by mid-next-year.
Spain: Dehesa first-phase drilling complete; Maria drilling from end of this month; 40 sq km Maria licence plus 30 sq km pending.
Mozambique: 1,500-2,000 m drilling from September; 200 tpd concentrator by end-2027.
demand_pricing: Management said gold price in Q1 was about Rs1,50,000 per 10 grams and improved in the current quarter, supporting holding inventory.
Tungsten prices up 622% and tantalum up 196% over the last year; lithium up 108%; graphite up 5% (management figures).
Management plans to sell Jonnagiri stock in the coming quarter; Q1 sales lagged production because the inauguration was on June 24.
Dore from Jonnagiri is refined in-house at a small refinery (cost about Rs4-5 Cr); Altyn Tor dore must go to a government refinery at LBMA price.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Jonnagiri profit margin well below the expected ~65% EBITDA, and what is the outlook for Jonnagiri and Kyrgyzstan revenue and profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low Q1 sales (59 kg) and initial expenses explain the low margin; 65-70% EBITDA margin expected in one to two quarters. Further clarity expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex estimate and funding plan for the project pipeline (about Rs2,000 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than Rs1,000 Cr is needed for the next two or three projects; funding via offtake arrangements for critical minerals, combined debt and equity; gold projects possibly 50:50 or 40:60 equity to debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhalukona be funded by a rights issue like the earlier Rs80 per share issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm a specific route; said the Rs137 Cr raise is a bridge and a larger QIP may follow once drilling outcomes are clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hutti Gold and Ganajur progress, and what is the legal position?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganajur is a mining lease with court proceedings pending; management cited recent judgments on restoring pre-2015 rights. Hutti is a prospecting licence, so it is more tedious; focus remains on Ganajur.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be dividends from Jonnagiri, and is a strategic promoter being sought?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend depends on Geomysore board; management doubts dividends this financial year. No decision yet on a large strategic promoter; the company remains professionally run.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not refine dore in Kyrgyzstan?
qa_highlights.answer: Kyrgyz law requires dore to be sent to a government refinery, which settles at LBMA price; no in-house refinery is possible there.

risks_watch: Jonnagiri margin normalisation: management guided EBITDA to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters, versus Q1 margins well below that; Q1 PAT of about Rs25 Cr on Rs87 Cr revenue (about 29%) is the key test next quarter.

Inventory realisation: about 80 kg gold equivalent (40 kg gold + 60 kg dore) unsold at quarter end, plus about 90 kg expected in Q2; sales timing depends on gold price and the Q1 consolidated inventory line was unchanged in P&L.

Funding gap: management cited more than Rs1,000 Cr needed for the next two to three projects (about Rs2,000 Cr overall in analyst framing), with Rs137 Cr raise subject to shareholder approval; mix of offtake, debt and equity not finalised; QIP may follow.
Ganajur court case: no regular hearing yet; outcome depends on court and on mining lease status; Hutti remains a prospecting licence.

Altyn Tor commissioning date not yet fixed (to be announced after Chairman visit next week); revised mine design and life-of-mine plan due by October 2026; Jonnagiri dividend to Deccan unlikely in FY27 per management.

Exploration catalysts due next quarter: Dehesa full results by mid-September, resource model by early October; Kalevala drilling from about 15 September; Chhattisgarh resource estimate and mining lease application next year.
key_quotes: As a snapshot, it has established us as clearly as producers.
I think the next quarter is going to be much bigger than this.
So, to stabilize to about 65%, 70% of EBITDA, I believe it will take another quarter or two.
Hence, I honestly, I doubt whether we get dividends in this financial year.
So, we cannot have a refinery of our own in Kyrgyzstan.
I think please give us time till the next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on production milestones, Kyrgyzstan commissioning and government support, but explicitly cautious on Q1 Jonnagiri margins, FY27 guidance (asked for one more quarter before firm numbers) and dividends, which management said it doubts this year. Evasive on promoter/strategic-investor plans and on exact funding split, saying decisions are not yet made.
